usage:
varlatch — self-host-first secrets and configuration

Usage:
  varlatch <command> --help                            # one command's usage (also: varlatch help <command>)
  varlatch --assisted <command>...                      # a coding agent drives the CLI (or VARLATCH_ASSISTED=1):
               run masks Secrets in the command's output by default and refuses one too short to mask
               (exit 78; --omit <NAME> leaves it out when the command does not need it), and refuses
               --allow-unmasked and --no-redact; values set/rotate never take a
               Secret's value from the command line, and replace an existing value only with --replace <ITEM>;
               values delete deletes only with --confirm <ITEM>; member remove and member leave always need --confirm;
               login with no method starts a device sign-in
  varlatch run --allow-unmasked <NAME>... -- <command>  # the human's override, outside assisted mode: shows only
               the named short Secrets; every other known Secret stays masked
  varlatch login --server <url> [--ttl <s>]              # browser passkey sign-in, in a browser on this machine
               (without --server: the server a command here uses, to sign in again. The first server you sign in
                to becomes the default for commands outside a repository; see varlatch server)
  varlatch login --server <url> --start [--ttl <s>] [--json]
               (device sign-in: prints an address and a code; approve it with your passkey in a browser on any
                device, then run --wait. The code lasts 10 minutes)
  varlatch login --server <url> --wait [--timeout <s>] [--json]
               (collects the approved sign-in and stores the credential; waits up to 60 seconds, at most 600;
                exit 75 when it is still pending: run --wait again)
  varlatch login --server <url> --token-stdin            # a credential from a pipe or file, e.g. from a password manager
  varlatch login --server <url> --token <credential>
  varlatch login --server <url> --oidc --org <organization> [--audience <aud>] [--oidc-token <jwt>] [--ttl <s>]
  varlatch logout [--server <url>|--all]                 # revokes server-side, removes locally
  varlatch server [--json]                               # the server commands here use, and the remembered default
  varlatch server use <url> [--json]                     # make a server you are signed in to the default
               (the default applies outside a repository only: a repository's varlatch.toml names its server)
  varlatch status [--json] [--probe]                     # stored credentials + repo context; offline unless --probe
  varlatch whoami [--server <url>] [--json]              # who this credential belongs to: identity, organization, credential
               (a person's or a machine's; uses VARLATCH_TOKEN, else the stored credential, as every command does)
  varlatch init [--org <slug>] [--project <slug>] [--server <url>] [--no-agent-files]
               (on a terminal, without --org or --project: asks for what is missing, signs in, creates the
                organization, project and environments you confirm, and offers to import .env files;
                off a terminal or in assisted mode both flags are needed, as before)
               (writes varlatch.toml with the server: --server, VARLATCH_SERVER, or the default server;
                also writes the files coding agents read, as agents install does; --no-agent-files skips them)
  varlatch agents guide [setup|run|agent-run|self-hosting|contract]
               (print the skill for coding agents, or one of its references: for any coding agent with a shell)
  varlatch agents install [--scope project|user] [--agent <name>]... [--guardrails] [--mcp] [--check|--remove] [--json]
               (write the skill to .agents/skills/varlatch and .claude/skills/varlatch, a marked block in AGENTS.md,
                and the adapters some coding agents need; --check exits 1 when the files differ, for CI;
                --remove takes back what install wrote; --guardrails also writes opt-in hooks and settings
                for Claude Code and Codex: accident prevention, not a boundary; --mcp adds a "varlatch mcp"
                server to the project's MCP files, for coding agents that should use MCP)
  varlatch agents hook --format <claude|codex>
               (the handler guardrail hooks call: reads a pre-tool-use event on stdin and denies reading .env files
                or the credential store, and printing the environment of a varlatch run)
  varlatch context [--json]
  varlatch env <use <name>|list [--json]>
  varlatch run [-e <env>] [--export-context] [--redact] [--no-redact] [--allow-unmasked <NAME>]... [--omit <NAME>]...
               -- <command> [args...]
               (--export-context: also give the command VARLATCH_RUN_CONTEXT, names only, for the Typed Accessor;
                --redact: mask the Secrets delivered to the command in its piped stdout and stderr,
                refused when either is a terminal, and with --agent-safe;
                --omit: leave an item stored here or in the Contract out of the command's environment, a copy
                inherited from this shell included; a Secret left out is not fetched, so it is not masked
                either, and a short one no longer stops an assisted run; another name exits 64)
  varlatch run --strict [--allow-inherited <NAME>]... [--omit <NAME>]... [--redact] -- <command> [args...]
               (validate exactly what the command receives; exit 78 and start nothing on any violation;
                --omit of an item required here is one; combine with --agent-safe for the agent-safe
                preflight: Secrets stay placeholders)
  varlatch run --agent-safe --agent <identity> --allow-host <host[:port]>...
               --target <NAME=header:<name>|query:<name>|json:<pointer>|form:<name>>... --omit <NAME>...
               [--broker-credential-file <path>] [--agent-network strict] [--ttl <s>]
               [--agent-metadata] -- <command>...
               (every stored Secret needs a --target or an --omit; it is substituted only there; the Agent gets its own
                empty configuration directory, so a varlatch command it starts never uses the operator's credential)
  varlatch request [-X <method>] [-H '<name>: <value>']... [-d <data>|@<file>|@-] [--json <data>|@<file>|@-]
                   [-o <file>] [-i] <https-url>
               (inside an agent-safe run: send the request through the Broker, which substitutes Secrets at their
                targets and scrubs the response; exit 0 on any whole response, 1 when the Broker refuses or the response
                is cut off, 77 when the Broker rejects the proxy credential, 69 unreachable)
  varlatch mcp [--server <url>] [--org <slug>] [--project <slug>] [-e <env>] [--allow-writes]
               (a Model Context Protocol server over stdio, for MCP hosts without a shell: read tools; --allow-writes
                adds non-secret writes; no tool returns or writes a Secret's value)
  varlatch validate [-e <env>] [--json]  (exit 1 invalid; 2 incomplete: items this identity may not read)
  varlatch values <set <ITEM> [<value> | -- <value>] [--replace <ITEM>]|list [--json]|delete <ITEM> [--confirm <ITEM>]|rotate <ITEM> [<new-value>] [--grace <s>] [--replace <ITEM>]|rotate-complete <ITEM>> [-e <env>]
                  set/rotate: --stdin | --from-file <path> | --generate <hex|base64|base64url:<bytes>|alnum:<chars>>,
                  or no value in a terminal for a hidden prompt
  varlatch import <file> [--dry-run] [--contract [--plain <NAME>]...] [--replace <NAME>]... [--delete-source] [--json] [-e <env>]
               (store a dotenv file's values without printing them; --contract adds new items to a Contract
                revision, Secrets unless --plain; --delete-source removes the file once every value is stored)
  varlatch contract <push --schema <.env.schema> | push --file <json> | activate <rev> | show> [--server <url>]
                   push [--semantics <version|latest>]   (pin Contract Semantics; default keeps the active version)
                   push [--json]                         (the new revision as JSON; show always prints JSON)
  varlatch types --out <file.ts|file.py> [--revision <id>] [--check]
                 (one TypeScript or Python module, by extension, with typed config and the Typed Accessor,
                  from the active Contract; --check exits 1 when the file is stale)
  varlatch sync push --platform <github-actions|coolify|convex> --base <owner|https://origin>
                     (--repo <name> [--gh-environment <name>] | --app <uuid> [--build-time true|false]
                      [--platform-expands NAME[,NAME…]] | --service <uuid> | nothing for convex: --base is the
                      deployment URL)
                     [--token-env VAR] [--map NAME[=DEST]]... [--exclude NAME|PREFIX*]... [-e <env>]
                     # client-side push for installations without server egress (ADR-0031)
  varlatch sync check --platform <github-actions|coolify|convex> --base <owner|https://origin>
                      (--repo <name> [--gh-environment <name>] | --app <uuid> | --service <uuid>
                       | nothing for convex)
                      [--token-env VAR] [--map NAME[=DEST]]... [--exclude NAME|PREFIX*]... [-e <env>] [--json]
               (does the platform hold the Environment's values? compared in memory, one status per key of
                the Contract: match, differs, missing-on-platform, extra-on-platform, unreadable, absent;
                never a value or a hash, so assisted mode allows it; exit 0 in sync, 1 drift, 2 not
                everything checked. Use it instead of printing the environment through varlatch run)
  varlatch admin backup create|verify|restore|status [--dir <compose-directory>]
  varlatch setup [--dir <compose-directory>] [--ingress public|tailnet|external] [--public-url <url>]
                 [--tailnet-machine <name>] [--tailscale-auth-key-file <f>] [--port <web-port>] [--no-wait]
                 [--tailnet-endpoint | --no-tailnet-endpoint] [--serve-cli | --no-serve-cli]
                 [--escrow passphrase|shamir|copy] [--escrow-passphrase-file <f>] [--attest]
                                                       # install: one command, resumable; --tailnet-endpoint
                                                       # lets approved devices read tailnet-protected values
                                                       # in the dashboard (HTTPS on port 8688 of the node);
                                                       # --serve-cli serves this installation's CLI and
                                                       # install scripts at /install.sh (off unless chosen)
  varlatch adopt [--dir <compose-directory>] [--apply] [--only <step>] [--revert <step>] [--secrets-dir <dir>]
                                                       # existing installation → managed, step by step
  varlatch move --public-url <url> [--ingress public|external] [--dir <compose-directory>]
                [--bek-file <path> | --bek-passphrase-file <path>] --kek-file <path> [--reenroll-hours <1-168>]
                [--yes] [--no-wait]                    # another public URL: archive, move, re-enrollment links
  varlatch move --abandon [--dir <compose-directory>]  # give up an open move: back to the old address
  varlatch admin reenroll (--all | --identity <id>...) [--hours <1-168>] [--dir <compose-directory>]
                                                       # one-time links: a new passkey on an existing identity
  varlatch admin security reset --org <organization> (--control <name>... | --all) [--json] [--dir <compose-directory>]
               (the host operator's way back: sets the named security controls to off and closes their open
                approvals; never touches deletion, passkeys or grants)
  varlatch admin unfreeze --org <slug> --confirm <slug> [--json] [--dir <compose-directory>]
               (the host operator's lift of an incident freeze, when nobody can approve it)
  varlatch admin outbound check [--allow <value>] [--org <organization>] [--json] [--dir <compose-directory>]
               (every configured webhook, Coolify and Convex Connection and OIDC issuer against the outbound policy,
                with the VARLATCH_OUTBOUND_ALLOW value that would allow the refused ones; DNS lookups only;
                exit 0 all allowed, 1 something refused, 2 something not resolved)
  varlatch doctor [--dir <compose-directory>] [--json] [--wait <s>] [--gate]
                                                       # read-only installation health on this host
  varlatch scan (--staged | <path>...) [-e <env>] [--json] [--baseline <file>] [--write-baseline]
                [--max-file-size <size>] [--max-total-size <size>]
               (look for this identity's Secrets in staged files or build output; one audited disclosure;
                exit 1 findings, 2 some files not scanned; never prints values or line contents)
  varlatch scan --install-hook [-e <env>]              # pre-commit hook running varlatch scan --staged
  varlatch scan --find-files [<dir>] [--json]
               (list files that look like copies of secrets by name: .env, .env.* except .env.example and
                .env.schema, *.pem, *.key; says whether Git ignores each; finds them by name and metadata,
                without reading their contents; needs no project or server; exit 1 files found, 2 search
                incomplete)
  varlatch invite <name> [--role member|admin]
  varlatch member <list [--json]|remove <member> --confirm <member>|leave --confirm <organization>|role <member> admin|member>
                                                       # people in the organization; former members are listed too
  varlatch member exposure <member> [--json]           # what a current or former member received, and what is still
                                                       # served; read-only, never a value (--json: NDJSON)
  varlatch tailnet <require --tailnet <tn> --tags tag:prod|requirements [--json]|remove <id>>
  varlatch audit <list [--json]|export>
  varlatch audit export --deleted-org <organization-id> [--server <url>]
                                                       # a deleted organization's audit log, for its readers
  varlatch org <list [--json]|create <slug> [name]> [--server <url>]
  varlatch org delete <slug> --confirm <slug> [--after <days>] [--server <url>]
                                                       # schedules the deletion (1-30 days, default 7) and
                                                       # freezes the organization until then
  varlatch org delete <slug> --approve <request-id> | --cancel <request-id> [--server <url>]
  varlatch org deletion <slug> [--json] [--server <url>]
                                                       # the open deletion request, if any
  varlatch org freeze <slug> --reason <text> --confirm <slug> [--server <url>]
                                                       # incident freeze: stops all access at once, reads
                                                       # included; no approval needed
  varlatch org unfreeze <slug> [--json] [--server <url>]
                                                       # lifts it: prints the approval URL and waits
  varlatch project <create <slug> --org <org> --server <url> [--managed]|list [--json]|rename <slug> <new-name>>
  varlatch project delete <slug> --confirm <slug> [--org <org>] [--server <url>]
                                                       # at once: erases every value of the project
  varlatch env-create <name> --tier <tier> | --parent <env> [--kind personal|preview]
  varlatch env-delete <name> [--confirm <name>]        # --confirm required for production-tier roots
  varlatch identity <list [--json]|rename <id> <new-name>|retire <id> [--confirm <name>]|reactivate <id>>
                                                       # --confirm required: retire revokes all credentials
  varlatch identity reach <id|name> [--json]           # what a machine's grants allow, per project and
                                                       # environment, with tailnet conditions; read-only
  varlatch credential <list <identity-id> [--json]|revoke <identity-id> <credential-id>>
  varlatch credential issue <identity-id> --name <name> [--ttl <s>] [--max-uses <n>] --out <file> [--json]
               (another credential for a service, workload, or broker identity, such as one per program;
                the token goes only to --out, a new file readable by you only, never to the output)
  varlatch audit-export show [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (the organization's audit export to object storage: destination, retention and Object Lock, how far it
                delivered, what is pending, the last error; needs organization.manage; never the key)
  varlatch audit-export create --endpoint <url> --region <region> --bucket <bucket> [--prefix <prefix>] [--path-style]
                               --access-key-id <id> [--secret-stdin | --secret-file <path>]
                               [--retention <compliance|governance>:<days>] [--from <beginning|now>] [--json]
               (copies every audit event of the organization to an S3-compatible bucket you control, with optional
                Object Lock retention; the destination is checked first, including that it refuses to overwrite;
                the secret access key comes from standard input, a file or a hidden prompt, never the command line;
                needs organization.manage and a person's credential)
  varlatch audit-export change [--endpoint <url>] [--region <region>] [--bucket <bucket>] [--prefix <prefix>]
                               [--path-style | --no-path-style] [--retention <mode>:<days> | --no-retention] [--json]
  varlatch audit-export change --access-key-id <id> [--secret-stdin | --secret-file <path>] [--json]
               (a new destination, a new key, or a shorter or removed retention always needs your approval with a
                trusted passkey; a longer or stronger retention does not; a new destination starts a new stream)
  varlatch audit-export remove --confirm <organization> [--json]
               (stops the copy and clears its key; what was delivered stays in the bucket; always needs your
                approval; in assisted mode only with --confirm, the human's decision)
  varlatch audit-export check [destination options] [--access-key-id <id> ...] [--retention <mode>:<days>] [--json]
               (checks a destination without saving anything: conditional writes, Object Lock, what the key may read;
                without a key, the export's own key against its own destination; exit 1 when the check fails)
  varlatch security status [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (the organization's security at a glance, as on the dashboard's Security page: each control's mode,
                what it counts and what enforce would change, its counts of the last 30 days, the admins' trusted and
                unconfirmed passkeys, credentials to review or expiring, tailnet requirements, and a checklist with
                links to the docs; parts you cannot read are named, not shown; read-only)
  varlatch security report [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (machine credentials never used, unused for 30 days, or without expiry, with their identity and
                last use, and service credentials expiring within 7 days or expired; reporting only: nothing is
                revoked or retired; needs identity.manage. With organization.manage, also the webhooks, connections
                and OIDC issuers this installation's outbound policy refuses, with why and since when)
  varlatch security controls [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (the organization's security controls: requirement-protection, admin-step-up, passkey-verification,
                credential-lifetime, each off, report or enforce; enforce only where the server offers it for that
                control)
  varlatch security set <control> <off|report|enforce> [--default-ttl <seconds>] [--max-ttl <seconds>] [--clear-config]
                        [--approval <id>] [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (needs organization.manage and a person's credential; tightening applies at once; loosening, such as
                report to off or a longer lifetime, needs your approval with a trusted passkey: the CLI prints an
                address, waits until you approved it in the dashboard, then sends the change again)
  varlatch --approval <id> <command>...                 # resume a command that needed your approval (step-up),
               after you approved it: waits for the approval (until it expires), then sends the command with it.
               In assisted mode the CLI never waits on its own: it prints the address, exits 75, and the command
               runs again with --approval <id> once the person approved
  varlatch --version                                   # CLI release; refresh it after every upgrade
  varlatch self-update [<version>] [--check [--json]] [--yes [--allow-unverified]] [--repo <owner/repo>]
                                                       # replace this CLI with a release build (checksum, signature)
  varlatch upgrade [<version>] [--dir <compose-dir>] [--check] [--repo <owner/repo>]
                   [--bek-file <path> | --bek-passphrase-file <path>] --kek-file <path> [--yes]
                   # backup-gated compose upgrade on this host (run where docker-compose.yml lives)

Exit status: 0 success; 1 failure; 64 the command line is wrong; 69 the server cannot be reached or is in
maintenance; 75 login --wait reached its deadline with the sign-in still pending, or an approval is still pending
(assisted mode) or expired; 77 not authenticated or denied, or an approval was cancelled, used or does not fit;
78 strict startup violation, or assisted mode cannot mask a Secret; 130 Ctrl-C stopped the wait for an approval.
Kept as before: validate 1 invalid, 2 incomplete; scan 1 findings, 2 not everything scanned; types --check 1 stale;
sync check 1 drift, 2 not everything checked;
run returns the command's own status once the command has started. agents install --check exits 1 when the files differ.

                revision, Secrets unless --plain; --delete-source removes the file once every value is stored)

Usage:
  varlatch init [--org <slug>] [--project <slug>] [--server <url>] [--no-agent-files]
               (on a terminal, without --org or --project: asks for what is missing, signs in, creates the
                organization, project and environments you confirm, and offers to import .env files;
                off a terminal or in assisted mode both flags are needed, as before)
               (writes varlatch.toml with the server: --server, VARLATCH_SERVER, or the default server;
                also writes the files coding agents read, as agents install does; --no-agent-files skips them)

Usage:
  varlatch invite <name> [--role member|admin]

Usage:
  varlatch login --server <url> [--ttl <s>]              # browser passkey sign-in, in a browser on this machine
               (without --server: the server a command here uses, to sign in again. The first server you sign in
                to becomes the default for commands outside a repository; see varlatch server)
  varlatch login --server <url> --start [--ttl <s>] [--json]
               (device sign-in: prints an address and a code; approve it with your passkey in a browser on any
                device, then run --wait. The code lasts 10 minutes)
  varlatch login --server <url> --wait [--timeout <s>] [--json]
               (collects the approved sign-in and stores the credential; waits up to 60 seconds, at most 600;
                exit 75 when it is still pending: run --wait again)
  varlatch login --server <url> --token-stdin            # a credential from a pipe or file, e.g. from a password manager
  varlatch login --server <url> --token <credential>
  varlatch login --server <url> --oidc --org <organization> [--audience <aud>] [--oidc-token <jwt>] [--ttl <s>]

Usage:
  varlatch logout [--server <url>|--all]                 # revokes server-side, removes locally

Usage:
  varlatch mcp [--server <url>] [--org <slug>] [--project <slug>] [-e <env>] [--allow-writes]
               (a Model Context Protocol server over stdio, for MCP hosts without a shell: read tools; --allow-writes
                adds non-secret writes; no tool returns or writes a Secret's value)

Usage:
  varlatch member <list [--json]|remove <member> --confirm <member>|leave --confirm <organization>|role <member> admin|member>
                                                       # people in the organization; former members are listed too
  varlatch member exposure <member> [--json]           # what a current or former member received, and what is still
                                                       # served; read-only, never a value (--json: NDJSON)

Usage:
  varlatch move --public-url <url> [--ingress public|external] [--dir <compose-directory>]
                [--bek-file <path> | --bek-passphrase-file <path>] --kek-file <path> [--reenroll-hours <1-168>]
                [--yes] [--no-wait]                    # another public URL: archive, move, re-enrollment links
  varlatch move --abandon [--dir <compose-directory>]  # give up an open move: back to the old address

Usage:
  varlatch org <list [--json]|create <slug> [name]> [--server <url>]
  varlatch org delete <slug> --confirm <slug> [--after <days>] [--server <url>]
                                                       # schedules the deletion (1-30 days, default 7) and
                                                       # freezes the organization until then
  varlatch org delete <slug> --approve <request-id> | --cancel <request-id> [--server <url>]
  varlatch org deletion <slug> [--json] [--server <url>]
                                                       # the open deletion request, if any
  varlatch org freeze <slug> --reason <text> --confirm <slug> [--server <url>]
                                                       # incident freeze: stops all access at once, reads
                                                       # included; no approval needed
  varlatch org unfreeze <slug> [--json] [--server <url>]
                                                       # lifts it: prints the approval URL and waits

Usage:
  varlatch project <create <slug> --org <org> --server <url> [--managed]|list [--json]|rename <slug> <new-name>>
  varlatch project delete <slug> --confirm <slug> [--org <org>] [--server <url>]
                                                       # at once: erases every value of the project

Usage:
  varlatch request [-X <method>] [-H '<name>: <value>']... [-d <data>|@<file>|@-] [--json <data>|@<file>|@-]
                   [-o <file>] [-i] <https-url>
               (inside an agent-safe run: send the request through the Broker, which substitutes Secrets at their
                targets and scrubs the response; exit 0 on any whole response, 1 when the Broker refuses or the response
                is cut off, 77 when the Broker rejects the proxy credential, 69 unreachable)

Usage:
  varlatch run --allow-unmasked <NAME>... -- <command>  # the human's override, outside assisted mode: shows only
               the named short Secrets; every other known Secret stays masked
  varlatch run [-e <env>] [--export-context] [--redact] [--no-redact] [--allow-unmasked <NAME>]... [--omit <NAME>]...
               -- <command> [args...]
               (--export-context: also give the command VARLATCH_RUN_CONTEXT, names only, for the Typed Accessor;
                --redact: mask the Secrets delivered to the command in its piped stdout and stderr,
                refused when either is a terminal, and with --agent-safe;
                --omit: leave an item stored here or in the Contract out of the command's environment, a copy
                inherited from this shell included; a Secret left out is not fetched, so it is not masked
                either, and a short one no longer stops an assisted run; another name exits 64)
  varlatch run --strict [--allow-inherited <NAME>]... [--omit <NAME>]... [--redact] -- <command> [args...]
               (validate exactly what the command receives; exit 78 and start nothing on any violation;
                --omit of an item required here is one; combine with --agent-safe for the agent-safe
                preflight: Secrets stay placeholders)
  varlatch run --agent-safe --agent <identity> --allow-host <host[:port]>...
               --target <NAME=header:<name>|query:<name>|json:<pointer>|form:<name>>... --omit <NAME>...
               [--broker-credential-file <path>] [--agent-network strict] [--ttl <s>]
               [--agent-metadata] -- <command>...
               (every stored Secret needs a --target or an --omit; it is substituted only there; the Agent gets its own
                empty configuration directory, so a varlatch command it starts never uses the operator's credential)

Usage:
  varlatch scan (--staged | <path>...) [-e <env>] [--json] [--baseline <file>] [--write-baseline]
                [--max-file-size <size>] [--max-total-size <size>]
               (look for this identity's Secrets in staged files or build output; one audited disclosure;
                exit 1 findings, 2 some files not scanned; never prints values or line contents)
  varlatch scan --install-hook [-e <env>]              # pre-commit hook running varlatch scan --staged
  varlatch scan --find-files [<dir>] [--json]
               (list files that look like copies of secrets by name: .env, .env.* except .env.example and
                .env.schema, *.pem, *.key; says whether Git ignores each; finds them by name and metadata,
                without reading their contents; needs no project or server; exit 1 files found, 2 search
                incomplete)

Usage:
  varlatch security status [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (the organization's security at a glance, as on the dashboard's Security page: each control's mode,
                what it counts and what enforce would change, its counts of the last 30 days, the admins' trusted and
                unconfirmed passkeys, credentials to review or expiring, tailnet requirements, and a checklist with
                links to the docs; parts you cannot read are named, not shown; read-only)
  varlatch security report [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (machine credentials never used, unused for 30 days, or without expiry, with their identity and
                last use, and service credentials expiring within 7 days or expired; reporting only: nothing is
                revoked or retired; needs identity.manage. With organization.manage, also the webhooks, connections
                and OIDC issuers this installation's outbound policy refuses, with why and since when)
  varlatch security controls [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (the organization's security controls: requirement-protection, admin-step-up, passkey-verification,
                credential-lifetime, each off, report or enforce; enforce only where the server offers it for that
                control)
  varlatch security set <control> <off|report|enforce> [--default-ttl <seconds>] [--max-ttl <seconds>] [--clear-config]
                        [--approval <id>] [--json] [--org <organization>] [--server <url>]
               (needs organization.manage and a person's credential; tightening applies at once; loosening, such as
                report to off or a longer lifetime, needs your approval with a trusted passkey: the CLI prints an
                address, waits until you approved it in the dashboard, then sends the change again)

Usage:
  varlatch self-update [<version>] [--check [--json]] [--yes [--allow-unverified]] [--repo <owner/repo>]
                                                       # replace this CLI with a release build (checksum, signature)

Usage:
  varlatch server [--json]                               # the server commands here use, and the remembered default
  varlatch server use <url> [--json]                     # make a server you are signed in to the default
               (the default applies outside a repository only: a repository's varlatch.toml names its server)

Usage:
  varlatch setup [--dir <compose-directory>] [--ingress public|tailnet|external] [--public-url <url>]
                 [--tailnet-machine <name>] [--tailscale-auth-key-file <f>] [--port <web-port>] [--no-wait]
                 [--tailnet-endpoint | --no-tailnet-endpoint] [--serve-cli | --no-serve-cli]
                 [--escrow passphrase|shamir|copy] [--escrow-passphrase-file <f>] [--attest]
                                                       # install: one command, resumable; --tailnet-endpoint
                                                       # lets approved devices read tailnet-protected values
                                                       # in the dashboard (HTTPS on port 8688 of the node);
                                                       # --serve-cli serves this installation's CLI and
                                                       # install scripts at /install.sh (off unless chosen)

Usage:
  varlatch status [--json] [--probe]                     # stored credentials + repo context; offline unless --probe

Usage:
  varlatch sync push --platform <github-actions|coolify|convex> --base <owner|https://origin>
                     (--repo <name> [--gh-environment <name>] | --app <uuid> [--build-time true|false]
                      [--platform-expands NAME[,NAME…]] | --service <uuid> | nothing for convex: --base is the
                      deployment URL)
                     [--token-env VAR] [--map NAME[=DEST]]... [--exclude NAME|PREFIX*]... [-e <env>]
                     # client-side push for installations without server egress (ADR-0031)
  varlatch sync check --platform <github-actions|coolify|convex> --base <owner|https://origin>
                      (--repo <name> [--gh-environment <name>] | --app <uuid> | --service <uuid>
                       | nothing for convex)
                      [--token-env VAR] [--map NAME[=DEST]]... [--exclude NAME|PREFIX*]... [-e <env>] [--json]
               (does the platform hold the Environment's values? compared in memory, one status per key of
                the Contract: match, differs, missing-on-platform, extra-on-platform, unreadable, absent;
                never a value or a hash, so assisted mode allows it; exit 0 in sync, 1 drift, 2 not
                everything checked. Use it instead of printing the environment through varlatch run)

Usage:
  varlatch tailnet <require --tailnet <tn> --tags tag:prod|requirements [--json]|remove <id>>

Usage:
  varlatch types --out <file.ts|file.py> [--revision <id>] [--check]
                 (one TypeScript or Python module, by extension, with typed config and the Typed Accessor,
                  from the active Contract; --check exits 1 when the file is stale)

Usage:
  varlatch upgrade [<version>] [--dir <compose-dir>] [--check] [--repo <owner/repo>]
                   [--bek-file <path> | --bek-passphrase-file <path>] --kek-file <path> [--yes]
                   # backup-gated compose upgrade on this host (run where docker-compose.yml lives)

Usage:
  varlatch validate [-e <env>] [--json]  (exit 1 invalid; 2 incomplete: items this identity may not read)

Usage:
